description: APSIM simulates biophysical processes in farming systems, particularly the economic and ecological outcomes of management under climate risk. It is also used for food security, climate change adaptation and mitigation, and carbon trading questions. It is a framework of biophysical modules for crops, pastures, trees and soil processes: water balance, nitrogen and phosphorus transformations, soil pH and erosion. Management modules hold the user's rules, and a simulation engine runs the modules together, from gene expression up to multi-field farms. It is developed by the APSIM Initiative, established in 2007, and new capability goes into APSIM Next Generation. Coverage is generic. Access: under the General Use Licence, APSIM is free of charge for public-good research and development, education, and policy or industry-good work whose outcomes are published. Improvements made by users belong to the APSIM Initiative and must be returned to it. Use without publishing the results, or in commercial products and services, needs a Special Use Licence. Caveats: the programming language and the download steps were not recorded from the pages read, and commercial use has licence conditions. For simulation it models crop, pasture and soil responses to drought, heat and management for farm resilience and adaptation studies. Related catalogue records include DSSAT, STICS, PCSE/WOFOST and the GGCMI outputs, where APSIM-UGOE is a participant.
